intro.text: A girl named Glorf, called Tress by everyone, who lives happily on Diggen's Point, a dismal island showered by spores from the Verdant Lunagree.
A young woman of Diggen's Point, nicknamed Tress for her wild hair, who washes windows for a living and collects cups.
A young window-washer from Diggen's Point, nicknamed Tress for her wild hair, who has left her island to rescue her beloved Charlie from the Sorceress.
A young woman from Diggen's Point who has become captain of the pirate ship Crow's Song on her quest to rescue Charlie from the Sorceress.
An eighteen-year-old from Diggen's Point, nicknamed Tress for her wild hair, who is captain and sprouter of the ship Two Cups.

items.text: Born to a peasant family on Diggen's Point and named Glorf after relatives, Tress was known by her nickname because of her wild hair. She washed windows, spending her earnings on pie ingredients to trade with sailors for cups. Working at the mansion, she kept meeting Charlie, the duke's son, who pretended to be a groundskeeper, and fell in love with him. While he was away courting princesses, he sent her four cups.

When the king and the duke refused to rescue Charlie from the Sorceress, Tress set out herself. With her father's help she conned her way aboard the Oot's Dream disguised as an inspector, but the smugglers aboard locked her up. Imprisoned, she met a rat named Huck. After the pirate ship Crow's Song attacked, she walked across the Verdant Sea to seek passage on it.

Aboard the Crow's Song, Fort, the cook only because he was the best of a bad lot, made sure Tress was fed. She traded her cooking for her meals and took over the galley, turning out food far beyond what the crew expected, to their delight.

Tress won a place on the Crow's Song by clinging to its side for fifteen minutes. She scrubbed decks, filled spore pouches for the cannons, and became the ship's sprouter. She learned Captain Crow wanted the crew to become deadrunners to force their loyalty. With Hoid's help she found midnight spores and used them to spy on Crow, learned to patch holes with spores, and found she could partly control spores with her thoughts.

Crow had first cared nothing for Tress, ordering her thrown overboard. Once Tress proved useful, Crow saw her instead as a possible cure for the spore gestation afflicting her, and underestimated her.

Some of the crew believed Tress was a King's Mask, despite her denials. She persuaded Crow to sail into the Crimson Sea, invented a flare gun that spread verdant spores, and saved the ship from the deadly rain until it reached the lunagree. Crow then discovered the planned mutiny, crushed it easily, and took Tress down beneath the spore sea.

Beneath the sea, Crow offered Tress to the dragon Xisis in exchange for a boon, and Tress made the same offer of herself. Each had to argue the other would be the better servant; Tress won by insisting she would do everything she could to escape. She bargained for gifts for her friends, including a new tablet for Fort, and returned as captain of the Crow's Song.

Tress had quickly befriended the gunner Ann, who taught her about sprouting and got her treatment from Ulaam when she blew up her own face. Returning from Xisis without Crow, Tress gave Ann spectacles to help with the micropsia that had troubled her all her life.

Tress caught Hoid throwing water and food overboard on Huck's orders, to stop the ship reaching the Sorceress. At the Midnight Sea, Tress and Huck failed to master the midnight essence, but Huck used his connection to the Sorceress to win passage. The Sorceress offered Charlie in exchange for Tress's two cups, but Tress realized this Charlie was fake and that Huck, cursed into a rat, was the real Charlie.

The crew came to rescue Tress, and she used a magical tablet to contact Fort. The Sorceress immobilized her, but Hoid, whom Tress as captain ordered to defend them, arrived just in time. Since Charlie's curse could not be undone, Tress used the threat of Hoid and the crew to make the Sorceress leave the planet in her tower, which was really a spaceship. Hoid then adjusted Charlie's curse.

Five months on, pardoned by the king, Tress, Charlie and the crew returned to Diggen's Point aboard their new ship, the Two Cups, with a royal writ letting people leave the island. Thanks to Hoid's change, Charlie was cured as long as he brought Tress home. They sailed off with her family and old crewmates, including Salay and the father she had found with Xisis's help, with Charlie as Tress's valet as they courted.

appearance.text: Tress's unruly hair, which she calls light brown though others call it wheat or honey, needs constant taming; she braids it with a ribbon, but strands float free. She wears a stolen inspector's uniform with a large red and gold coat. She collects cups avidly, loved showing new ones to Charlie, and took favorites with her on her journey.
Tress has green eyes. Ulaam admires them and offered to trade one for a deep blue eye, which she declined.

personality.text: Tress is thoughtful and kind, with a tendency to fixate that shows in her cup collection and her sprouting. She cares deeply for her crewmates and risks her life for them, and they love her for it. New to sprouting, she respects spores without letting fear stop her, bonding with midnight essence and lifting a ship with verdant spores.

Tress is brave and naive about the wider world, and sees the best in people. She tried to face the midnight essence alone rather than risk her crew, and when Laggart asked her to kill him after Crow's defeat, she chose forgiveness instead.
